# unleash_feature (Resource)

Creates a feature flag and manages its metadata (type, description and impression data). Strategies, variants and whether the flag is enabled in each environment are intentionally not managed here: change those in Unleash.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A long-lived kill switch, created alongside the service that checks it.
# Its strategies and whether it is on in each environment are managed in Unleash.
resource "unleash_feature" "checkout_kill_switch" {
  name        = "checkout.kill-switch"
  project     = "default"
  type        = "kill-switch"
  description = "Turns off checkout when the payment provider is degraded"
}

# Import an existing flag as <project>/<name>, or just <name> for the default project
import {
  id = "default/search.new-ranking"
  to = unleash_feature.new_ranking
}

resource "unleash_feature" "new_ranking" {
  name            = "search.new-ranking"
  type            = "experiment"
  impression_data = true
  # destroying this resource also deletes the flag from the archive, freeing its name
  archive_on_destroy = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the feature flag. Must be unique across the instance, including archived flags, and may only contain letters, numbers and the characters `-._~`. Changing it creates a new flag.

### Optional

- `archive_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true` (the default), destroying this resource archives the flag, as deleting a flag in the Unleash UI does, so it can be revived later. When `false`, the flag is also permanently deleted from the archive, which frees up its name.
- `description` (String) A description of the feature flag.
- `impression_data` (Boolean) Whether to emit [impression data](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/impression-data) for this flag. Defaults to `false`.
- `project` (String) The project the feature flag belongs to. Defaults to `default`. Changing it creates a new flag.
- `type` (String) The [type](https://docs.getunleash.io/concepts/feature-flags#feature-flag-types) of the feature flag, for example `release`, `experiment`, `operational`, `kill-switch` or `permission`. Defaults to `release`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The name of the feature flag.
